hajar-zamzam.title: Hajar in the valley: “Then He will not abandon us”
subCategories: A mother alone with her child
hajar-zamzam.eventDescription: Ibrahim left Hajar and her infant son Isma‘il in an uncultivated valley near the House, with no one and no water. She followed him asking: Where are you going, leaving us? He did not turn back. She said: Did Allah command you to do this? He said: Yes. She said: “Then He will not abandon us.” When the water ran out and the child grew thirsty, she did not sit and wait; she ran between al-Safa and al-Marwah seven times searching, and relief came with the water of Zamzam. The Prophet ﷺ said: “That is the running of people between them.”
hajar-zamzam.historicalContext: Narrated at length by al-Bukhari from Ibn ‘Abbas; it marks the beginning of Makkah's settlement.
hajar-zamzam.problemType: Finding yourself alone in a hard situation (a mother on her own, living abroad, starting from zero, losing the breadwinner)
hajar-zamzam.responseType: Certainty that Allah will not abandon you, together with determined effort instead of passive waiting
principles: Certainty does not cancel effort: she said “He will not abandon us,” then ran seven times
Allah makes the effort of the weak an everlasting rite
The right question in hardship: is this something that pleases Allah?
Relief may come from where you were not looking
modernApplications: If you are a mother raising your children alone, say with certainty: “Then He will not abandon us,” then strive with all you can
Abroad or starting from zero: run between the “Safa” and “Marwah” of your life (work, searching, asking for help) and do not give up
Do not wait for relief sitting down; movement is part of trust
Remember that every pilgrim running today follows the footsteps of a lone woman who did not despair
notToApplyTo: The story does not justify a father or husband abandoning his responsibilities; Ibrahim's leaving was by Allah's command and special revelation
behaviorObservations: She asked the essential question and then was at peace
Her trust did not turn into passive waiting
She repeated the attempt seven times
whatToAvoid: Trust without effort
Despair after the first attempt
hajar-zamzam.reflection: She said “Then He will not abandon us” — and then she ran. That is trust: a heart at peace and feet that strive.

himar-khamr.title: “Do not curse him”: the man repeatedly brought in for drinking
himar-khamr.eventDescription: A man named ‘Abdullah, nicknamed Himar, used to make the Prophet ﷺ laugh, and he had been flogged for drinking wine many times. One day he was brought in and flogged, and a man among the people said: O Allah, curse him — how often he is brought in! The Prophet ﷺ said: “Do not curse him, for by Allah, I know only that he loves Allah and His Messenger.” In another narration he said: “Do not be helpers of Satan against your brother.”
himar-khamr.historicalContext: In Madinah; narrated by al-Bukhari from ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab.
prophetTraits: Seeing the good in the sinner
himar-khamr.problemType: An addiction or bad habit that keeps returning despite attempts, and feeling you do not deserve Allah's mercy — or a relative afflicted with it
himar-khamr.responseType: Separating the sin from the person, preserving the good in them, and not helping Satan against them by taunting
principles: A repeated sin does not cancel love of Allah and His Messenger in the heart
Taunting and cursing help Satan against the sinner
Applying what is right does not contradict mercy to the person
In every person there is good that can be built on
modernApplications: If you are struggling with addiction, do not believe the voice saying “you're a hypocrite, there's no point”; your love for Allah is real and is the start of the road
Seek specialised treatment for addiction; it is taking the means, not weak faith
If a relative is addicted, criticise the act, not the person, and remind them of the good in them
Avoid the places, people and times that lead you to the habit
notToApplyTo: Mercy to an addict does not mean enabling them, giving them money or tolerating violence from them; boundaries and treatment are necessary
behaviorObservations: He applied the punishment, and that did not stop him defending the man's dignity
He publicly mentioned the good he knew in him
He stopped the cursing immediately
whatToAvoid: Cursing or taunting the sinner
Despairing of yourself after a relapse
himar-khamr.reflection: Your repeated sin does not erase your love for Allah; make that love a rope to hold on to, not an accusation to be ashamed of.

sadaqa-sariq.title: Charity that landed in a thief's hand: “Perhaps he will refrain”
sadaqa-sariq.eventDescription: The Prophet ﷺ told of a man who said: Tonight I will give charity. He put it in the hand of a thief, and in the morning people were saying: Charity was given to a thief! He said: O Allah, to You belongs praise. Then he gave again and it fell into the hand of a prostitute, then into the hand of a rich man. He was told: As for your charity to the thief, perhaps he will refrain from stealing; the prostitute, perhaps she will refrain from her immorality; and the rich man, perhaps he will take a lesson and spend from what Allah has given him.
sadaqa-sariq.historicalContext: An agreed-upon hadith narrated by Abu Hurayrah.
sadaqa-sariq.problemType: You helped someone and then found they did not deserve it, exploited you or did not thank you, and you regret giving
sadaqa-sariq.responseType: Counting the intention with Allah, trusting that good is never lost, and looking more carefully for the deserving in future
principles: The reward is for the intention, not the outcome
Good may change even the one who did not deserve it
Do not let a bad experience stop your giving
Looking for the deserving is required, but a mistake in it does not lose the reward
modernApplications: If you helped someone who turned out to be lying, say: O Allah, to You belongs praise — and do not regret it
Next time look more carefully, through trusted charities, without stopping your giving
Do not expect thanks from those you helped; your giving was for Allah
Your giving to someone in the wrong may be the cause of their change; do not belittle its effect
notToApplyTo: This does not mean continuing to give to someone you know uses the money for the forbidden or to cause harm
behaviorObservations: He praised Allah each time without complaint
He did not stop giving after the first time
He was shown an effect he could not see
whatToAvoid: Stopping doing good because of a bad experience
Reminding of favours or hurting after giving
sadaqa-sariq.reflection: Your charity reached Allah before it reached anyone's hand; do not grieve over the hand that received it.

wahshi.title: Wahshi, Hamzah's killer: “Can you keep your face away from me?”
subCategories: Accepting the repentance of one who hurt you
participants: Hamzah ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib (may Allah be pleased with him)
wahshi.eventDescription: Wahshi killed Hamzah, the Prophet's ﷺ uncle, at Uhud, and Quraysh mutilated his body. Years later Wahshi came as a Muslim. The Prophet ﷺ accepted his Islam and did not punish him. He asked: “Are you Wahshi? Did you kill Hamzah?” Wahshi told him what happened, and he said: “Can you keep your face away from me?” He forgave completely, but did not bind himself to a closeness that would renew his pain. Wahshi later went out and killed Musaylimah the Liar, and used to say: I killed the best of people and the worst of people.
wahshi.historicalContext: Narrated at length by al-Bukhari from Wahshi himself; he came as a Muslim with the envoys of al-Ta'if.
wahshi.problemType: Someone who hurt you deeply has repented or apologised; you have forgiven them but cannot bear being close to them
wahshi.responseType: Complete forgiveness of the right, with the right to keep a distance that protects the heart
emotionsAddressed: Guilt at not being able to be close
Being torn between forgiveness and boundaries
principles: Forgiveness does not mean returning to the same closeness
Acknowledging feelings is honesty, not weakness
Accepting another's repentance does not require forgetting the pain
The repentant may do great good afterwards, so do not judge their end
modernApplications: If you have forgiven someone but cannot bear to see them, you are not a hypocrite; keep a courteous distance
Do not force yourself into a close relationship with someone who hurt you badly to prove you have forgiven

Do not stop others from accepting or dealing with them

behaviorObservations: He accepted his Islam without punishment
He was honest about his feelings
He did not prevent him from doing good afterwards
whatToAvoid: Forcing a closeness that reopens the wound

waswasa-sarih.title: “That is clear faith”: when unwanted thoughts frighten you
waswasa-sarih.eventDescription: Some Companions came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: We find in ourselves thoughts that one of us considers too terrible to speak of. He said: “Do you really find that?” They said: Yes. He said: “That is clear faith.” A man came and said: I have thoughts that I would rather be burnt to charcoal than speak of. He said: “Praise be to Allah who has reduced Satan's plot to whispering.” And he taught them: when these thoughts come, “let him seek refuge in Allah and stop.”
waswasa-sarih.historicalContext: Hadith in Sahih Muslim and Sunan Abi Dawud.
waswasa-sarih.problemType: Disturbing intrusive thoughts about belief, purity or prayer that frighten you and make you feel guilty or like a disbeliever
waswasa-sarih.responseType: Reassurance that hating them is a sign of faith, with seeking refuge, stopping, and not engaging with them
principles: Hating the thought and being alarmed by it is proof of faith

A person is not held accountable for compulsive thoughts
The cure for whisperings is ignoring them, not repeated reassurance
modernApplications: When the thought comes, say: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan; I believe in Allah — then get busy with something at once

With whisperings about purity and prayer: act on your first impression and do not repeat
If the whispers disrupt your life, it is often obsessive-compulsive disorder, and psychological treatment is effective and legitimate
notToApplyTo: This is for unwanted compulsive thoughts, not intellectual doubt where a person is seeking an answer; that is treated with knowledge and dialogue with scholars
behaviorObservations: He reassured them first before teaching them
He praised Allah that Satan's plot went no further than whispering
He gave them a two-step cure: seek refuge and stop
whatToAvoid: Arguing and debating with the whispers
Repeatedly asking for reassurance
waswasa-sarih.reflection: The thought that frightens you and that you hate is not from you; it is testimony that there is faith in your heart rejecting it.

safiyya-ghiba.title: “If it were mixed with the sea, it would pollute it”: one small word of backbiting

sahl-ayn.eventDescription: ‘Amir ibn Rabi‘ah saw Sahl ibn Hunayf bathing and, admiring the fairness of his skin, said: I have never seen anything like today! Sahl collapsed on the spot. hummara.title: “Who has distressed this one over her young?”: mercy to birds and animals
hummara.eventDescription: The Companions were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey and saw a small bird with two chicks; they took the chicks, and the mother came fluttering over them. The Prophet ﷺ came and said: “Who has distressed this one over her young? Return her young to her.” He saw an ant colony that had been burned and said: “Who burned this?” They said: We did. He said: “No one should punish with fire except the Lord of the fire.” He entered a garden and found a camel weeping; he stroked it and said to its owner: “Do you not fear Allah regarding this animal that Allah has given you? It has complained to me that you starve it and overwork it.”

hummara.problemType: Cruelty to animals (by you, your children or others), or uncertainty about the rights of pets

modernApplications: Teach your children not to disturb birds' nests or torment cats

If you see an animal being tormented, intervene wisely or report it to the relevant authority
notToApplyTo: This does not prevent killing harmful insects and animals in a non-torturous way when needed

whatToAvoid: Belittling an animal's pain

hummara.reflection: “Who has distressed this one over her young?” — a Prophetic question revealing that mercy cannot be divided.
